items.title: Keith Ingham interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: She says, 'my uncle Fred wrote that.' ... 'I remember Uncle Fred,' she said

ctx.x: And a Gershwin painting on the wall? That’s not bad. You think New York is a pretty good place to be. You know I love New York anyway. And I met Burton Lane, you know, the great theater composer. You know this whole tradition of the American musical coming out of theater and then going into the movies and then the songs are taken up by bands you know. It’s just a wonderful continuity. And it still lives on in a lesser way. I mean I was playing, and I have a steady gig in New York, I’m lucky to say that because…
Thanks ASCAP, for sending those checks.
